skill.name: wiki-changelog
skill.description: Generates structured changelogs from git commit history, grouped by time period and categorized by change type.
skill.summary: Turn recent git commits into clear changelog sections for users and maintainers.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Static analysis found no suspicious patterns in the single prompt-only skill file. Manual review found no prompt injection language, data exfiltration intent, or instructions that request unsafe tool use.

content.user_title: Generate Repository Changelogs from Git History
content.value_statement: Teams need quick, readable summaries of repository activity. This skill reviews git history and organizes commits into clear changelog sections.
actual_capabilities: Reviews git commit history for recent repository activity.
Groups changes by daily and weekly time periods.
Classifies commits into features, fixes, refactoring, documentation, configuration, dependencies, and breaking changes.
Combines related commits into concise user-facing descriptions.
Highlights breaking changes with migration notes when evidence exists.
limitations: Requires access to repository git history in the current workspace.
Depends on commit messages and available project documentation for accuracy.
Does not publish release notes or modify repository files by itself.
Cannot infer hidden product impact when commits lack useful context.

use_cases.title: Prepare Release Notes
use_cases.description: Create a structured changelog before tagging a new version or sharing a product update.

use_cases.title: Summarize Sprint Activity
use_cases.description: Review recent commits and explain development progress in clear categories.

use_cases.title: Update Project Documentation
use_cases.description: Convert repository changes into concise wiki or README update notes.

prompt_templates.title: Recent Changelog
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple repository update.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a changelog for the recent commits in this repository. Group the changes by type and keep the descriptions user-facing.

prompt_templates.title: Weekly Development Summary
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a time-based activity report.
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize the last two weeks of git history. Group changes by week, then classify each item as feature, fix, refactor, documentation, config, dependency, or breaking.

prompt_templates.title: Release Candidate Notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Create release candidate notes from commits since the last tag. Highlight breaking changes, migration notes, and user-facing improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Audience-Specific Changelog
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a tailored changelog.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a changelog for product stakeholders. Merge related commits, avoid internal implementation noise, and explain the user impact of each change.

output_examples.input: Generate a changelog for the last week.
output: Features: Added account export support and improved onboarding status messages.
Fixes: Resolved failed login redirects and corrected duplicate notification handling.
Documentation: Updated setup instructions to match the current environment variables.

output_examples.input: Summarize commits since the last release.
output: Breaking Changes: Renamed the project configuration option and included migration guidance.
Dependencies: Updated core packages to supported versions.
Refactoring: Simplified repository services without changing user-facing behavior.

best_practices: Run the skill from the repository root so git history and project context are available.
Ask for a specific date range or tag range when preparing release notes.
Review breaking change sections before publishing the changelog.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague commit messages as final release notes without review.
Do not include internal-only refactors when the audience needs product changes.
Do not assume a breaking change exists unless commit history or code context supports it.

faq.question: Does this skill change repository files?
faq.answer: No. The skill describes a workflow for analyzing git history and writing changelog text.

faq.question: Can it generate release notes for a specific version?
faq.answer: Yes. Ask for commits since a tag, branch point, or date range.

faq.question: Does it need network access?
faq.answer: No. The skill is designed to use local git history and local project documentation.

faq.question: How does it categorize changes?
faq.answer: It groups commits into features, fixes, refactoring, documentation, configuration, dependencies, and breaking changes.

faq.question: Will it detect every user impact?
faq.answer: Not always. Clear commit messages and project documentation improve the quality of the changelog.

faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
